newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Doutor says coffee price won't dent profit.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Doutor says coffee price won't dent profit.

text.p: Japanese coffee shop operator Doutor Coffee Co says it has covered its coffee supplies at around 100 cents a lb until July shipments, and the surge in coffeee bean prices earlier this year will not damage its profits.
"We've covered coffee at the previous price level until July, so we are not feeling pressures on our profits," Doutor Coffee Co president Hiromichi Toriba told Reuters in a recent interview.
Doutor has forecast a parent current profit of 2.70 billion yen in the year to March 31, against a profit of 1.82 billion the previous year.

The Japanese firm imports nearly 3,000 tonnes of coffee beans per year, he said. "We've experienced the ups and downs of coffee prices in the past 35 years, but never had serious damage to our profits. We're optimistic this time, too," Toriba said.
The May contract of New York coffee futures market hit a high 209.50 cents a lb on March 5, up from a low of 102.60 cents on December 6.
The price surges were driven by tight supplies at roasters, strikes in Colombia, and doubts about the size of this year's crop in Brazil.
